source.title: Standard Treatment Workflow (STW) for Dermatophytoses
source.publisher: Department of Health Research, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India

sections.label: Signs That Need Specialist Attention
items: Very extensive infection covering large areas of the body
No improvement at all after 4 weeks of regular treatment
Infection that keeps coming back repeatedly despite completing full treatment
Infection present during pregnancy or in someone with liver, kidney, or heart disease
Suspected or known history of prolonged use of steroid-containing creams, these can significantly worsen fungal infections and make them very difficult to treat

sections.label: Self-Care at Home
items: Take a daily bath with regular soap and normal temperature water
Dry the skin thoroughly after bathing, especially the area between the toes and skin folds
Wash clothes separately in hot water and dry them inside-out in the sun
Do not share towels, clothes, or undergarments with others
Do not re-wear clothes before washing them
Keep nails trimmed short, infected nails are fragile and can spread the fungus
Avoid walking barefoot in public places such as swimming pools or community bathing areas
Wear cotton socks and change them daily
Do not use any steroid-containing cream (often sold as combination creams at chemists), these make fungal infections much worse
Do not stop treatment as soon as the itching improves, always complete the full course as the infection is still present
Do not self-medicate; this can make the infection harder to treat later

sections.label: See a Doctor
items: Any itchy, ring-shaped, scaly rash on the skin, groin, feet, or hands
Nail discoloration, thickening, or crumbling
Infection that has not responded to treatment after 4 weeks
Infection spreading to other family members
Infection in the groin, palms, or soles
Scaling along the creases of palms or soles, or dried blisters on feet
If you are pregnant or have a chronic illness before starting any treatment

sections.label: Refer to Specialist or Tertiary Centre
items: Very extensive body-wide disease
No improvement after 4 weeks of regular treatment with correct antifungals
Infection not clearing despite prolonged treatment and good compliance
Recurrent infection
Presence of conditions that affect treatment choices: pregnancy, liver disease, kidney disease, or heart disease

review.notes: All antifungal drug names, dosing schedules, and topical cream formulations excluded per AIRA refusal policy. Important patient safety warning included: steroid-containing OTC creams worsen fungal infections.
